description: Occupy Mars is a solo team from Universitas Widyatama, Bandung, Indonesia. I’m an Information Systems student who enjoys working with Earth observation data, data visualization, and web development. Excited to spend this weekend turning NASA satellite data into something useful. Happy to connect and exchange ideas with fellow participants!
summary: ApiKala ("Api" = fire, "Kala" = time/season in Indonesian) turns 26 years of NASA FIRMS active-fire hotspots into one consistent burning-activity calendar for Indonesia. MODIS (1 km, since 2000) and VIIRS (375 m, since 2012) cannot be compared directly: in Indonesia, raw VIIRS records about 5 times more hotspots than MODIS. ApiKala converts every month to "MODIS-equivalent hotspots" using island- and month-specific factors learned from 2012-2021, when both sensors flew together. Users pick a province, draw a box or enter coordinates, and see the fire season, the worst years, and whether this month is above the historical median. Leave-one-year-out tests reproduce MODIS within 1.5% bias (R2 = 0.97, versus +406% for raw VIIRS), and the results track official burned area from Indonesia's Ministry of Forestry (r = 0.83 over 225 province-years). Monthly tables and raw hotspots can be downloaded as CSV. This matters now: Suomi NPP stopped delivering data on 2 Nov 2026 and MODIS is near its end, so the long record must be harmonized to stay usable.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

ApiKala is a web app that shows a burning-activity calendar (year x month, 2000 to today) for any area of Indonesia: a province, an island, a box drawn on the map, or a point with a radius. It shows the peak fire month, the worst years, and whether the current month is below normal, normal, above normal or far above normal compared with the historical median (pro-rated for the month in progress). An anomaly view, a fire-season chart and annual totals support the calendar. Users can download a monthly CSV for their area and fetch raw hotspots from the FIRMS API with their own MAP_KEY. The interface is in English and Bahasa Indonesia, with colour-blind-friendly colour ramps.

WHY IT MATTERS

NASA's challenge notes that MODIS and VIIRS records cannot be compared directly, leaving fire managers without a consistent picture. In Indonesia, joining them naively makes hotspot counts jump about 5 times after 2012 (raw VIIRS bias +406% against MODIS). With Suomi NPP ending on 2 Nov 2026 and MODIS near its end, a harmonized record is needed to keep the 26-year baseline usable. Our data and official statistics both show 2026 as a severe fire year in Indonesia.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Download NASA FIRMS country yearly files for Indonesia (MODIS C6.1 Terra and Aqua; VIIRS S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21) and use the FIRMS API for the current year.

2. Keep MODIS confidence >= 30, VIIRS nominal/high, vegetation fires only (type 0).

3. Count hotspots per 0.25-degree grid cell and month; map each cell to one of 34 provinces and 7 island groups.

4. Convert everything to MODIS (Terra + Aqua) equivalents. From 2012: VIIRS x k[island, month], where k = sum of MODIS / sum of VIIRS over 2012-2021 (before the Terra/Aqua orbit drift). Months without full S-NPP coverage use NOAA-20 converted to S-NPP; Terra-only months (Nov 2000 to Jun 2002) are scaled to Terra + Aqua.

5. Validate twice: leave-one-year-out (R2 = 0.97, bias 1.5% at island x month level) and an external check against official burned area from SIPONGI KEMENHUT (r = 0.83 on log scales over 225 province-years; national r = 0.97).

TOOLS

Python (pandas, NumPy) in Google Colab for the pipeline; HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SVG and Leaflet for the web app; GitHub and GitHub Pages for code and hosting. Source code: https://github.com/asepggwp/apikala

SI assistance: Claude Opus 5.5 (medium effort) by Anthropic helped draft the code, documentation and logo; all data processing was run and checked by the team.

CREATIVITY AND DESIGN CHOICES

Harmonization factors vary by island and month instead of one global ratio, because the MODIS/VIIRS gap differs between peatland fires in Kalimantan and small agricultural fires in Java. The calendar answers one practical question at a glance: "is this month unusual here?" Results are checked against an independent official dataset, not only against the satellites themselves.

LIMITATIONS AND NEXT STEPS

Hotspot counts are not burned area, and clouds or smoke hide some fires. The 0.25-degree grid (about 28 km) approximates area boundaries. Current-year data come from the FIRMS API and may be revised. Next: district-level areas, alerts when a month crosses "far above normal", an offline version for field teams, and applying the method to other countries.
